quizzes.title: Key terms and ideas
quizzes.intro: Ten checks on the three drawings — design, draft and peg plan — and the vocabulary of denting.

questions.q: On the design (point paper), what do the columns and rows represent?
options: Columns are healds, rows are picks
Columns are ends, rows are picks
Columns are picks, rows are ends
Columns are dents, rows are healds
questions.explain: The design has ends across (columns) and picks up (rows). Columns of healds belong to the peg plan, not the design.

questions.q: What does the draft show?
options: Which healds rise on each pick
How many ends go through each reed dent
The colour order of the warp
questions.explain: The draft (threading) has one row per heald frame and marks the heald each end is drawn on. Which healds rise on each pick is the peg plan.

questions.q: What does the peg (lifting) plan show?
options: Which healds rise on each pick
The interlacing of every end with every pick
questions.explain: The peg plan has one column per heald and one row per pick and marks the healds that lift. The end-by-end interlacing is the design itself.

questions.q: Which rule decides how many healds a weave needs?
options: One heald per end in the repeat
One heald per pick in the repeat
The number of different end movements
The number of ends per dent
questions.explain: Ends that move identically share a heald, so the number of healds equals the number of different end movements. A repeat of 8 ends may need only 4 healds.

questions.q: For a straight draft the peg plan is the design itself.
questions.explain: With a straight draft end 1 is on heald 1, end 2 on heald 2 and so on, so lifting heald n on a pick is the same as lifting end n; the peg plan and the design coincide.

questions.q: A denting plan states
options: The order of healds in the draft
How many ends are drawn through each reed dent
questions.explain: Denting is the grouping of ends through the reed — 2, 3 or 4 per dent in the lecture's table.

questions.q: Why should the ends in one dent not all lift together?
options: It would break the reed wires
It would leave reed marks in the cloth
It would double the picks per inch
questions.explain: If every end in a dent rises as one group, the reed wire splits the group visibly and the cloth shows reed marks; the lecture gives this as the reason for choosing the denting.

questions.q: In the draft, where does end 5 of a straight-drafted 3/1 twill on four healds go?
questions.explain: End 5 moves exactly like end 1, so both are drawn on heald 1; the threading reads 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4.

questions.q: In the pointed draft 1 2 3 4 3 2 the peg plan has to be changed from the ordinary 2/2 twill.
questions.explain: The lecture shows that only the draft turns back; the peg plan stays a plain 2/2 twill. The pointed effect comes from the threading.

questions.q: The term ends per dent refers to the
options: Number of ends drawn on one heald
Number of ends lifted on one pick
Number of ends passing through one gap in the reed
Number of ends in one repeat
questions.explain: A dent is one space between reed wires; ends per dent counts the ends threaded through it.

quizzes.title: Formulas and relationships
quizzes.intro: Healds from drafts, peg-plan dimensions, the denting table and the link between EPI, ends per dent and reed count.

questions.q: A peg plan for a 4-heald weave with a 4-pick repeat has how many columns and rows?
questions.explain: One column per heald and one row per pick: 4 × 4. The number of ends in the repeat does not enter the peg plan.

questions.q: Reed count (dents per inch) is found from
questions.explain: Reed count = EPI ÷ ends per dent, as the lecture states with reference to Weaving Calculations 11. Multiplying would give far too many dents.

questions.q: According to the lecture's table, how many ends per dent are used for plain weave and why?
options: 2, one up and one down in each dent
questions.explain: Two ends per dent put one rising and one sinking end in each dent, which avoids reed marks and matches the 2-end repeat.

questions.q: For a 2/1 twill the table gives 3 ends per dent because
options: The whole 3-end repeat fits in one dent
questions.explain: Three ends per dent put a whole 2/1 repeat in each dent, so every dent has two up and one down on every pick.

questions.q: Why does a 5-end satin use 2 and 3 ends per dent alternately?
options: Because its repeat does not divide by 2 or 4
Because satin needs a very coarse reed
questions.explain: Five ends cannot be split evenly into dents of 2 or 4, so 2 and 3 alternate (average 2.5) to fit the 5-end repeat.

questions.q: If the ends per inch are kept constant and the ends per dent are raised from 2 to 4, the reed count
questions.explain: Reed count = EPI ÷ ends per dent, so doubling the ends per dent halves the dents per inch needed.

questions.q: A 3/1 twill and a 2/2 twill are both dented 4 ends per dent in the lecture's table.
questions.explain: Both repeat on 4 ends, so a whole repeat goes through each dent.

questions.q: In the draft of a straight-drafted weave repeating on 8 ends with 8 different end movements, how many rows does the draft have?
questions.explain: One row per heald, and eight different movements need eight healds, so the draft has eight rows.

questions.q: Which of the following changes the number of healds required?
options: Changing the number of different end movements in the weave
questions.explain: Healds are counted by distinct end movements; denting and reed count affect the reed, not the healds.

questions.q: The average ends per dent for a 5-end satin dented 2 and 3 alternately is 2.5.
questions.explain: (2 + 3) ÷ 2 = 2.5 ends per dent on average, the figure the table quotes.

quizzes.title: Worked calculations
quizzes.intro: Heald counts from drafts and reed calculations from EPI and ends per dent.

questions.q: A warp is set at 60 ends per inch in plain weave, dented 2 ends per dent. What reed count (dents per inch) is required?
questions.explain: Reed count = EPI ÷ ends per dent = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 dents per inch.

questions.q: A 2/1 twill is to have 72 ends per inch, dented 3 per dent. What is the reed count?
questions.explain: 72 ÷ 3 = 24 dents per inch.

questions.q: A 5-end satin is set at 100 ends per inch and dented 2 and 3 alternately (average 2.5). What reed count is needed?
questions.explain: 100 ÷ 2.5 = 40 dents per inch.

questions.q: A 2/2 twill warp has 3,840 ends and is dented 4 ends per dent. How many dents does it occupy?
A reed has 32 dents per inch and the weave is dented 3 ends per dent. What are the ends per inch?
questions.explain: EPI = reed count × ends per dent = 32 × 3 = 96 (the reed-count formula rearranged).

questions.q: A straight-drafted 3/1 twill is woven on 4 healds. How many ends are drawn on each heald in a warp of 2,400 ends?
questions.explain: With a straight draft the ends are shared equally: 2,400 ÷ 4 = 600 ends per heald.

questions.q: The pointed draft 1 2 3 4 3 2 repeats on 6 ends. In a warp of 1,800 ends, how many ends are drawn on heald 1?
questions.explain: Heald 1 appears once in every 6-end repeat, so 1,800 ÷ 6 = 300 ends. Healds 2 and 3 each take twice as many.

questions.q: The lecture's 3/1 twill design is drawn 8 ends × 8 picks on 4 healds. How many columns does its peg plan have?
questions.explain: The peg plan has one column per heald, so 4 columns, even though the design is 8 ends wide.

questions.q: Reading the draft 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4, which heald carries end 7?
questions.explain: Counting along the threading, end 7 is the seventh entry, heald 3.

questions.q: A plain-weave reed is 40 dents per inch at 2 ends per dent. The same reed is to be used for a 2/1 twill at 3 ends per dent. What EPI results?
questions.explain: EPI = 40 dents × 3 ends per dent = 120. At 2 per dent the same reed gave 80.

quizzes.title: Applied in practice
quizzes.intro: Drawing-in and reed decisions in the weaving shed: what to do when the healds, the reed or the denting do not fit.

questions.q: A dobby has only four heald frames free. Which of these can be drawn in?
options: A weave with eight different end movements
questions.explain: The pointed draft uses only healds 1–4, so four frames suffice. The other weaves have more than four different end movements.

questions.q: A plain-weave cloth shows fine lengthwise lines in the cloth that follow the reed wires. What is the likely cause?
options: The denting lets all the ends in a dent lift together
The picks per inch are too high
The draft is pointed instead of straight
questions.explain: Reed marks come from ends in a dent rising as one group; the lecture says the denting is chosen so the ends in a dent are not all lifting together.

questions.q: A 5-end satin is being drawn in. The drawer-in wants to use 4 ends per dent throughout. What is the problem?
options: The 5-end repeat does not divide by 4, so dent groups and repeats drift apart; use 2 and 3 alternately
The reed count would be too high
Satin must be dented 1 per dent
questions.explain: The lecture's table dents 5-end satin 2, 3 alternately precisely because 5 is not divisible by 2 or 4; a constant 4 per dent would not match the repeat.

questions.q: The store only has a 24-dent reed, but the order needs 72 ends per inch in a 2/1 twill. What should the weaver do?
options: Dent 3 ends per dent, giving 24 × 3 = 72 EPI
Dent 2 ends per dent and accept 48 EPI
Dent 4 ends per dent, giving 96 EPI
questions.explain: 3 per dent on a 24-dent reed gives exactly 72 EPI and matches the 3-end repeat of a 2/1 twill, as the table recommends.

questions.q: If the drawer-in uses a straight draft by mistake instead of the pointed draft 1 2 3 4 3 2, the cloth will still show the pointed twill because the peg plan is correct.
questions.explain: The pointed effect comes from the draft; with a straight draft and the same 2/2 peg plan the loom weaves an ordinary 2/2 twill.

questions.q: A weave engine reports that a design needs 12 healds, but the loom has 8. What does this tell the designer?
options: The design has 12 ends per repeat
The design has 12 different end movements and must be simplified or moved to a bigger dobby
questions.explain: Heald count equals distinct end movements. Reducing the ends per repeat does not help unless the number of different movements falls to 8 or fewer.

questions.q: A 2/2 twill is dented 4 per dent as recommended. What does each dent contain on every pick?
options: Two ends up and two down
One end up and three down
It varies from pick to pick
questions.explain: A whole 2/2 repeat per dent means two of the four ends are lifted on every pick, so no dent ever rises as one block.

questions.q: The sett of a plain-weave order is raised from 60 to 80 EPI while the same 2-per-dent denting is kept. What must change in the loom?
options: The reed, from 30 to 40 dents per inch
The number of healds, from 2 to 4
questions.explain: Reed count = EPI ÷ ends per dent: 60 ÷ 2 = 30 and 80 ÷ 2 = 40, so a 40-dent reed is needed. The weave and healds are unchanged.

questions.q: Why is the number of healds, not the number of ends, the figure to check before accepting a design for a loom?
options: Because looms have a limited number of heald frames, while each frame can carry many ends
Because ends are counted by the reed
Because the peg plan ignores ends
Because healds decide the picks per inch
questions.explain: Hundreds of ends can share one heald; it is the count of frames that the loom's dobby limits.

questions.q: Changing the ends per dent changes the reed required but not the draft or the peg plan.
questions.explain: Denting concerns only the reed; the draft and peg plan depend on the weave's end movements and lifting order.

quizzes.title: Challenge review
quizzes.intro: Harder questions linking design, draft, peg plan and reed, with the slips that catch students out.

questions.q: A student says the draft shows which healds lift on each pick. What has been confused?
options: The draft with the peg plan: the draft gives the heald of each end, the peg plan the healds lifted per pick
The draft with the denting plan
questions.explain: The student has described the peg plan. The draft is the threading of ends on healds.

questions.q: A pointed draft 1 2 3 4 3 2 is used over a warp of 1,200 ends. How many ends are on heald 3?
questions.explain: Heald 3 appears twice in every 6-end repeat: 1,200 ÷ 6 = 200 repeats × 2 = 400 ends. Heald 1 carries only 200.

questions.q: With a straight draft on four healds, lifting healds 1, 2 and 3 on a pick means
options: Ends 1, 2 and 3 (and every fourth end after them) are up and heald 4's ends are down — a 3/1 pick
Only ends 1, 2 and 3 of the whole warp are up
questions.explain: Every end drawn on healds 1–3 rises across the full width, giving three up and one down per four ends, which is a 3/1 twill pick.

questions.q: A warp of 4,800 ends in 5-end satin is dented 2 and 3 alternately (average 2.5 ends per dent). How many dents are used?
The 4,800-end satin warp above occupies 1,920 dents and is to be woven 60 inches wide in the reed. What reed count is needed?
questions.explain: 1,920 dents ÷ 60 inches = 32 dents per inch (equivalently 80 EPI ÷ 2.5).

questions.q: A weave repeating on 8 ends always needs 8 healds.
questions.explain: It needs as many healds as there are different end movements; the lecture's 3/1 twill drawn on 8 ends uses only 4 healds.

questions.q: The ends per dent are chosen to match the weave repeat or divide into it. For a 2/2 twill, which denting would therefore be a poor choice?
questions.explain: Three does not divide the 4-end repeat, so the dent groups would drift against the weave; 2 and 4 both divide 4.

questions.q: A straight-drafted weave and a pointed-drafted weave use the same 2/2 twill peg plan. In what way do their drafts differ?
options: Only the pointed draft turns back after heald 4
The pointed draft uses more healds
The straight draft has more ends per repeat
questions.explain: Both use four healds; the straight draft reads 1 2 3 4 1 2 3 4 while the pointed one reads 1 2 3 4 3 2 and returns.

questions.q: A loom is set with a 36-dent reed at 2 ends per dent for plain weave. A designer wants to weave a 3/1 twill at the same 72 EPI with the recommended 4 per dent. What reed is required?
questions.explain: 72 EPI ÷ 4 ends per dent = 18 dents per inch; the plain-weave reed at 36 would need to be changed.

questions.q: Why does the lecture say the weave engine can generate the draft and peg plan automatically from the design?
options: Because ends with identical movements can be grouped on healds and the lifts of those healds read off the design
Because every weave uses a straight draft
questions.explain: Grouping identical end movements gives the draft, and the lifting of each group on each pick gives the peg plan — a mechanical procedure a program can follow.
